text:
Situation: Epinephrine is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21. The prior shortage first posted 2012-04-27 is resolved. Current stock across three sites ranges from 3.3 to 25 days of supply, with the lowest coverage at Corvale East for the 0.3 mg/0.3 mL syringe (3.3 days) and 0.15 mg/0.3 mL syringe (4.9 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA's records show the 2012-04-27 shortage posting. An import alert 66-66 for Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG (FEI 3002806556) was published 2009-09-30, 940 days before that posting. FDA inspection 808119 at that plant ended 2012-11-12 classified OAI, 199 days after the posting. A Warning Letter was issued 2013-05-06 to the same plant, 374 days after the posting. FDA inspection 762138 at Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) ended 2012-01-04 classified VAI, 114 days before the posting. Later FDA inspection 1064827 at Hospira ended 2018-08-15 classified OAI, with the OAI classification letter dated 2020-04-22, 2917 days after the posting.

Our position: Supply is adequate at Corvale General and Corvale Lakeside but tight at Corvale East for syringe presentations. No active FDA shortage exists. The preferred sourcing route is a supplier not on FDA's shortage list.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to place orders with Viatris Specialty LLC for Corvale East syringe presentations; requires P&T committee approval.
2. Buyer to evaluate kaleo, Inc. as a secondary source for syringe presentations; requires P&T committee approval.
3. Buyer to qualify American Regent, Inc., Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC, and Amneal Pharmaceuticals Private Limited as backup sources; requires P&T committee approval.
4. Buyer to monitor daily usage at Corvale East and trigger inter-site transfers from Corvale General if days-on-hand fall below 3; requires pharmacy director approval.

Not recommended: No allocation, rationing, or clinical protocol changes at this time.
